newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore jet fuel actively offered at firm prices.
newsitem.headline: Singapore jet fuel actively offered at firm prices.

text.p: Singapore oil products prices firmed up on Monday along with crudes with several offers being offered at high values while gas oil was mixed, traders said.

They said at least four majors offered November-lifting jet fuel starting at high levels but later lowered due to few bids. The first major started offering 180,000 barrels of November 17-20 jet fuel at $31.50 a barrel. But another major later offered to as low as $30.60 for Nov 10-14. A trader made bids at $30.30 for early November.
Traders said the abundant offers mirrored the plentiful supplies and lack of buying interest in jet fuel.

Apart from majors with fob Singapore cargoes, two traders are bringing in MidEast jet fuel cargoes in November. A European trader has a 30,000 tonnes in storage and is targetting the Japanese market. But traders said, other than the 30,000 tonnes bought by a Japanese refiner on Friday at $1.50 a barrel over Singapore quotes for mid-November delivery c+f, no other interest were seen from Japan. "The Japanese are comfortable with their inventories and there are still no signs of cold weather," a trader said. India has issued its December kerosene tender which closes on Oct 31. Swaps gas oil rose 5 cents on crudes but physical offers were lowered to $30.40 for Nov 16-20.

China was rumoured to have bought November gas oil at $240 a tonne c+f but some traders discounted it as too high. They said this is a seller's asking level. Naphtha firmed with crude but traders expected prices to dip early next week. They said other than two S.Korean refiners seeking November cargoes, north Asian demand, particularly from Japan, was not so strong. Talks on Singapore barrels were thin as there was no demand, said a Japanese trader. Premiums were firm at 60-70 cents a barrel. A cargo of 95-octane unleaded gasoline was heard traded at 10 cents per barrel fob over Singapore quotes lifting November 27-December 1. --Singapore Newsroom (+65-8703086)
